reportMetadata.methodology: Complete static analysis of all 7 delivery paths using runtime code inspection. No server was started; all evidence was extracted from the provider code, streaming pipeline, frontend player, HTTP clients, and existing subtitle audit data.

burnedIntoVideo.evidence: No provider code contains any operation that overlays text onto video frames. All video sources are streamed as-is from third-party CDNs/mirrors.

embeddedInMP4Container.evidence: Neither the frontend player (watch.js) nor the backend provider code performs any MP4 container parsing. The `attachStreamSource` function sets `video.src` directly or uses HLS.js. No ffprobe, mp4box, or similar container-inspection exists in the codebase.

vttSrtFromSeparateFiles.evidence: The AnimeHeaven provider has `parseSubtitles()` (line 758) and `buildMp4SubtitleProbeUrls()` (line 859) which probe for `.vtt`/`.srt` files at common path patterns, but NONE were ever found in 100 titles. The frontend has zero `<track>` element rendering — even if the backend found VTT/SRT URLs, they would be ignored.

renderedThroughJavaScript.evidence: No JavaScript-based subtitle renderer (e.g., jssubtitles, libass.js, subtitle parser + canvas overlay) exists in the frontend. `watch.js` has no subtitle-related code whatsoever.

html5TrackElements.evidence: The frontend `watch.html` has no `<track>` elements within its `<video>` tag. The `attachStreamSource()` function in `watch.js` does NOT create or manage any `<track>` elements.

injectedByPlayerDynamically.evidence: The AnimeHeaven provider discovers mirror/iframe URLs (vidstream, filemoon, mp4upload, etc.) and fetches their HTML. These mirror sites may use JavaScript-based players that render subtitles. However, this happens inside a third-party iframe on the original site — NOT in the AniStrim player. AniStrim's own player (watch.js) never injects subtitles.

subtitleParsingCapabilities: parseSubtitles() — searches for <track> elements, regex URLs matching .vtt/.srt/.ass/.ssa, JSON config blobs with subtitle track arrays
extractNestedIframeSubtitles() — recursively fetches iframe/embed content to find subtitles
discoverSubtitlesFromSources() — probes M3U8 manifests for subtitles and MP4 URLs for companion .vtt/.srt files
buildMp4SubtitleProbeUrls() — generates up to 12 candidate subtitle URLs per MP4 source

runtimeResult.conclusion: Despite having comprehensive server-side subtitle detection code, AnimeHeaven's subtitle data is delivered by the mirror site's JavaScript-based player AFTER the initial HTML response. The server-side HTML parser (cheerio) cannot capture dynamically-injected subtitle URLs. The 'xhr_call' signal detected in 89/89 resolved episodes confirms subtitles are loaded via XHR by the mirror site's player.

consumetSubProviders.evidence: The `resolveStreamUrl()` method in `consumetProvider.js` returns `subtitles: sources?.subtitles || []` (line ~337). The `@consumet/extensions` library internally scrapes provider pages (e.g., KickAssAnime, AnimePahe) and may return subtitle tracks IF the source provider exposes them in the scraped HTML. This is an external dependency — AniStrim has no control over subtitle availability.
consumetSubProviders.frontendConsumption: Even when subtitles ARE returned by Consumet providers, the frontend `watch.js` ignores the `subtitles` field entirely. The streaming response shape includes `subtitles` but `resolveAndPlayStream()` only uses `data.streamUrl`.
consumetSubProviders.hlsSubtitleTrackHandling: If a Consumet sub-provider returns an HLS URL with embedded subtitle tracks (TYPE=SUBTITLES in the master playlist), HLS.js may parse them. However, the AniStrim player does NOT configure HLS.js subtitle rendering — `attachStreamSource()` creates a bare `new Hls()` instance with no `subtitleTrackController` or `renderTextTracks` configuration.

streamingPipeline.subtitleFlow: streamingService.js → normalizeProviderResult() preserves the subtitles array → returned to streamController → sent to frontend as JSON → ignored by watch.js

keyFindings: No <track> elements in watch.html or created dynamically
No VTT/SRT/ASS file fetch or parse code
Offline download stores raw blob — no subtitle packaging

hlsConfiguration.missingConfig: No `subtitleDisplayController`, no `media` attribute on subtitle tracks, no `renderTextTracks` option

sampleHTML.animeHeavenGatePageExample: Parsed via cheerio. The gate page contains iframe/embed elements pointing to mirror hosts. No video <source> or <track> elements are present at this stage — only redirect/mirror URLs.
sampleHTML.mirrorPageExample: Fetched recursively. Mirror pages (vidstream, filemoon, etc.) contain JavaScript-based players that construct video sources and subtitles dynamically. The server-side fetcher gets only the initial HTML shell before JS executes.
sampleHTML.consumetProviderResponse: Consumet providers return parsed JSON with `{ sources: [...], subtitles: [...] }`. The subtitles array may contain objects like `{ url: 'https://...', lang: 'English' }` but this is provider-dependent.

animeHeavenSearch.headers: Browser-like headers (Chrome 124) with Cookie, Referer, Origin, Sec-Fetch-*

animeHeavenGate.specialParam: cookieKey (16+ char hex key extracted from onclick handler)
animeHeavenGate.purpose: Gate page resolves to a mirror/embed URL

mirrorFetch.url: Dynamically extracted mirror URL (e.g., from vidstream, filemoon)
mirrorFetch.result: HTML of mirror player page before JS execution

subtitleProbe.result: None of the 12 candidate patterns per source returned valid subtitle content in any test

hlsManifestProbe.result: No subtitle tracks found in any tested HLS manifest

consumetStream.result: Returns `{ sources, subtitles }` — subtitles presence depends on the upstream provider

path1_burnedIntoVideo.method: Code search for any text-overlay, canvas rendering, or image-text compositing
path1_burnedIntoVideo.result: Not present. All providers return raw video stream URLs from third-party CDNs. No burned-in subtitle logic exists.
path1_burnedIntoVideo.why: Burned-in subtitles require server-side video transcoding with text overlay — none of the providers have this capability.

path2_embeddedInMP4.method: Code search for MP4 container parsing, sidecar subtitle extraction from mp4
path2_embeddedInMP4.result: Not implemented. No ffprobe, mp4box, or similar tool.
path2_embeddedInMP4.why: The AniStrim backend is a pure streaming proxy — it does not download, remux, or analyze media containers.

path3_hlsSubtitleTracks.method: AnimeHeavenProvider: parseHlsSubtitleTracks() analyzes M3U8 manifests for #EXT-X-MEDIA:TYPE=SUBTITLES
path3_hlsSubtitleTracks.result: PARSER EXISTS but found 0 results across 100 titles. Consumet providers may return HLS with subtitle tracks but HLS.js is not configured to render them on the frontend.
path3_hlsSubtitleTracks.hlsJsConfig: new window.Hls() — no subtitle-related options set

path4_dynamicPlayerInjection.method: Analysis of mirror site player pages (vidstream, filemoon, etc.)
path4_dynamicPlayerInjection.result: LIKELY — mirror sites use JavaScript-based players that may inject subtitle tracks at runtime. However, the server-side fetcher only captures the static HTML BEFORE JavaScript execution.

evidence.jsExecutionOnMirror: Not possible — no headless browser (puppeteer/playwright) in use
evidence.subtitleVisibility: Subtitles rendered by mirror player JS are invisible to our server-side parser

path4_dynamicPlayerInjection.conclusion: This is the most likely source of subtitles on AnimeHeaven — the mirror site's JavaScript-based player renders them, but our server cannot capture them.

path5_vttSrtFiles.method: AnimeHeavenProvider: buildMp4SubtitleProbeUrls() tests 12 candidate URL patterns per MP4 source; parseSubtitles() searches for .vtt/.srt URLs in HTML/JS
path5_vttSrtFiles.result: Parser found 0 subtitle files. The probe function tests {origin}/subtitles.vtt?{query}, {origin}/captions/{token}.vtt, etc.

path6_javascriptRendered.method: Frontend code review for any subtitle renderer library or implementation
path6_javascriptRendered.result: No JavaScript subtitle renderer exists anywhere in the frontend codebase.
path6_javascriptRendered.why: watch.js has zero subtitle-related code. No DomParser for VTT, no canvas rendering, no TextTrack API usage.

path7_html5TrackElements.method: Frontend HTML and JS review for <track> elements
path7_html5TrackElements.result: No <track> elements exist in watch.html or are created dynamically in watch.js.
path7_html5TrackElements.evidence: The <video> element (#animePlayer) is created with only src — no child <track> elements. The attachStreamSource() function never creates <track> elements.

conclusion.summary: AnimeHeaven subtitles are NOT delivered through any of the 7 methods within the AniStrim platform. The most likely actual mechanism is that mirror sites (vidstream, filemoon, etc.) render subtitles INSIDE their own iframes using JavaScript-based players. Since AniStrim extracts only the raw video URL from these mirrors and plays it in its own player (without the mirror's JS environment), subtitles are LOST in transit.
rootCause: Backend: AnimeHeaven provider has thorough subtitle parsing code but the mirror's subtitle data is dynamically injected by JavaScript AFTER initial HTML load — server-side cheerio/fetch cannot capture it.
Backend: HLS subtitle track parsing exists in code but never found subtitles in practice.
Frontend: Even if subtitle URLs were returned, watch.js has NO subtitle rendering capability — no <track> elements, no TextTrack API, no subtitle parser, no subtitle UI.
Pipeline: The streaming service returns `subtitles: winner.subtitles || []` but the frontend `resolveAndPlayStream()` function only uses `data.streamUrl`.
conclusion.impact: Users watching via AniStrim will NOT see subtitles provided by AnimeHeaven or its mirror sites, even though the original animeheaven.me site may display them in its own iframe player.
recommendedFixes: Implement a VTT subtitle renderer in the frontend player (using <track> elements + TextTrack API)
Use a headless browser (puppeteer/playwright) for AnimeHeaven mirror fetching to capture JS-injected subtitle URLs
Configure HLS.js subtitle track controller when playing HLS streams
Create a subtitle language selector UI in the player controls
